# A hull-exact, strictly nonheavy obstruction to shear-optimized projection bounds

This note concerns projection coefficients, not a counterexample to OC.
The mechanism is the nonaffine hollow-base lift already characterized in
`candidate 254a4d13e061ac3e`. The new conclusion is a
uniform quantitative obstruction after **every continuous shear and every
primitive integer direction**.

## 1. The actual convex body and all of its integer fibers

Fix L>0 and epsilon>0. In R^2_z times R_x define

    P={0,1,2} times {0,1},
    C=conv{(z,L z_1 z_2): z in P} + ({0} times [0,epsilon]).

The four lifted corner points are affinely independent: the alternating
sum of their x-coordinates is 2L, whereas the same alternating sum of
their base coordinates vanishes. Hence C is a compact convex body in
R^3. Its integer projection is exactly P. Every point of P lies on one
of the two horizontal boundary edges of its rectangular projection.
Convex combinations giving a point on either such edge use only points
of that edge, and the displayed lifting is affine on each edge.
Consequently the actual integer fibers are exactly

    C_z=[L z_1 z_2,L z_1 z_2+epsilon],  z in P.             (1)

In particular, with S=C intersect (Z^2 times R),

    C=conv(S),    M=H_1(S)=6epsilon,
    max_z |C_z|=epsilon < M/2^2=3epsilon/2.                (2)

There are no discarded boundary fibers or zero-volume fibers.

## 2. Two elementary planar facts

**Four-point area fact.** For arbitrary U,V,W in R^2,

    area conv{0,U,V,U+V+W}
       >= (1/2) max(|det(U,W)|,|det(V,W)|).               (3)

For the first bound, the triangles with common base [0,U] and third
vertices V and U+V+W have signed determinants delta=det(U,V) and
delta+det(U,W). If the signs differ, the triangles have disjoint
interiors and their summed area is at least |det(U,W)|/2. If the signs
agree, the larger triangle has area at least |det(U,W)|/2. Degenerate
determinants cause no exception. Interchanging U and V proves the
second bound.

**Integral-versus-sampling fact.** Let Q be a convex polygon in
R_w times R_x whose vertices all have integer w-coordinates. Let
f(w)=length{ x:(w,x) in Q }. Then

    sum_(j in Z) f(j) >= area(Q).                         (4)

Indeed, on its nondegenerate support [l,r], l,r are integers, and f is
continuous and piecewise affine with all breakpoints at integers. Thus

    area(Q)=f(l)/2 + sum_(l<j<r) f(j) + f(r)/2.

The same inequality is immediate if Q has zero area. This proof retains
any nonzero endpoint sections.

## 3. Uniformity over all shears and primitive directions

Apply an arbitrary lattice-preserving continuous shear

    x'=x-a z_1-b z_2.                                    (5)

An additional continuous translation is immaterial. The shear changes
no fiber length and preserves all ambient halfspaces.

Let v=(p,q) be any primitive nonzero integer vector. The quotient lattice
Z^2/Zv is identified with Z by

    w=q z_1-p z_2,

because gcd(p,q)=1. Thus its coefficient A_v is precisely the sum of
the x'-section lengths over integer w of the actual projected body.
The projections of the four lower lifted corners are

    0, U, V, U+V+W,
    U=(2q,-2a), V=(-p,-b), W=(0,2L).

Their convex hull lies in the projected body. Equation (3) gives

    area(projected body)
      >= L max(2|q|,|p|) >= L.                            (6)

Every vertex of the projected body comes from a projected vertex of C,
so every such vertex has integer w-coordinate. Applying (4),

    A_v(C after shear) >= L max(2|q|,|p|) >= L.            (7)

This is simultaneous for every a,b in R and every primitive v. It
therefore also applies to every column of every unimodular integer
basis selected after the shear. In particular,

    inf_(shears, primitive v) A_v/M >= L/(6epsilon).       (8)

Taking L/epsilon arbitrarily large disproves a finite universal upper
bound for this optimized coefficient ratio even at fixed (n,d)=(2,1),
under C=conv(S), equal positive fiber volumes, and strict nonheaviness.

## 4. The full-rank coefficient also cannot be normalized away

The quotient obtained by freeing both integer directions is the interval
spanned by the sheared heights of the four corners, enlarged by
[0,epsilon]. Denote its length by A_{12}. The four lower heights h_00,
h_20,h_01,h_21 satisfy

    h_00+h_21-h_20-h_01=2L.

If their range is R, the absolute value of this alternating sum is at
most 2R. Hence

    A_{12} >= L+epsilon.                                 (9)

Equality is attained by a=L/2,b=L: the four lower heights are
0,-L,-L,0. Thus even the full-rank quotient coefficient has an exact
unbounded minimum ratio (L+epsilon)/(6epsilon). It is independent of
which unimodular basis is used to free both integer directions.

## 5. Scope and the remaining arithmetic distinction

The body has a hollow base: its rectangle has no relative-interior
integer points, although it has six sampled bases and no heavy fiber.
The affine displacement of a two-fiber example can be removed by (5),
whereas the alternating lift 2L here is invariant under every such
shear. This is why canonical hull normalization does not repair the
coefficient comparison.

The example does not exclude a proof that uses the integer-anchored
edges separately, or uses the actual halfspace structure rather than
only projection coefficients. Indeed each horizontal edge carries
exactly half of M, and its three interval fibers have an affine centroid
graph. The example satisfies OC; no deficient center is claimed.

All assertions above have the explicit scope n=2,d=1. They suffice to
refute any bound asserted simultaneously for all n,d. No padding or
untracked change of Hausdorff normalization is needed.

For contrast, the corresponding coefficient cannot diverge this way in
integer rank one once the hull-generated integer projection has at least
three points. Translate that projection to {0,...,N}, N>=2, choose one
point in each endpoint fiber, and shear so these two points both become
0. Every intervening fiber then contains 0. For k=floor(N/2), mixing
fiber j<=k with the point 0 at N, or fiber j>=k with the point 0 at 0,
gives

    C_j subset [N/min(k,N-k)] C_k.

Because the body is the hull of its integer fibers, its whole continuous
shadow satisfies A<=[N/floor(N/2)]^d |C_k|<=3^d M. For even N the factor
is 2^d. This elementary bound is too weak for the OC constant; it only
distinguishes the higher-rank hollow mechanism in (8).
